method.text: Every page read in ascending physical-page order using pypdf layout extraction, then reread in the page image as needed.
method.visual: Every physical page 205-309 individually opened with view_image at 900 x 1350, rendered directly from the reading PDF by Ghostscript at 150 dpi. No contact-sheet or file-existence substitution.
method.image_numbering: Preview sequence 001 maps to reading-PDF physical page 205; physical page = sequence + 204.
method.coverage_limit: Editorial and visual review of the reading PDF only. Not an independent recertification of all historical, technical, legal or financial claims; specific pending verification is labeled. No manuscript or PDF edits made.

findings.quote: where P is the number of parameters in billions
findings.reason: Multiple mid-section pages have large empty lower areas before an unbreakable figure or mechanism/rule/practice block. Page 253 is particularly disruptive: only a brief continuation appears above most of a blank page. This fragments reading and adds apparent unfinished space. Chapter-ending whitespace is not included.
findings.suggested_correction: Audit figure sizing and keep-together rules as spreads. Allow safe breaks inside long precedent blocks and resize or reposition suitable figures while preserving readable labels. Keep each caption with its figure. Re-review changed pagination rather than merely checking that no text disappeared.
findings.verification: confirmed by full-page visual inspection; CSS cause not yet established

findings.quote: NIST glossary, air gap None of those means
findings.reason: Inline linked source labels use ordinary body type in the PDF and are not enclosed or punctuated. Readers must guess where a source title ends and the argument resumes. The Seiko title also crosses a page break into Between 1970.
findings.suggested_correction: Give citation links a consistent print treatment, such as parenthesized short source labels or numbered endnotes. Preserve URLs and distinguish citations from ordinary links. Verify grayscale as well as the reading PDF.
findings.verification: confirmed visually; not a claim that citations are absent

findings.quote: If the second line feels like a betrayal of the first, you've drawn it correctly.
findings.reason: The exercise asks readers to protect a craft or standard, then treats discomfort or betrayal as proof of success. That can dismiss a legitimate ethical or quality concern and gives the reader no way to distinguish productive discomfort from real compromise.
findings.suggested_correction: Consider: The two lines may look very different. Check that the offering funds what you mean to keep without undermining it. Keep the challenge to purity tests, but make success observable.

findings.quote: don't try to build a big, complicated suburban house. Build a shouse
findings.reason: The preceding paragraph explicitly makes an existing apartment or other housing form a valid answer. This unconditional command immediately narrows the whole reader route to an owned or leased shop-house, even though the chapter later offers shared benches without construction.
findings.suggested_correction: Make the route conditional: If your plan calls for a workshop beside your home, a shouse is one way to keep both compact and under one roof. Retain the concrete approved-use steps for readers choosing that route.
findings.verification: internal comparison within the same page and page 243

findings.quote: The chapter’s budget belongs to its fiction.
findings.reason: The diagram and caption point to a chapter budget, but the current Chapter 13 gives no numerical build budget. The only scene-budget reference concerns buying chimney components new. This looks like a leftover from an earlier edition and sends readers looking for a missing estimate.
findings.suggested_correction: Replace the diagram footer and caption clause with a direct boundary: Fictional example; site-specific design and costs. Update source and print SVG variants together through the established asset workflow.
findings.verification: confirmed against full current chapter text and both SVG labels

findings.quote: faster than any central capacity could have been built
findings.reason: The history presented supports rapid mobilization of existing distributed capacity, but not this absolute counterfactual comparison with every possible centralized alternative. It is stronger than the cited evidence as described in the chapter.
findings.suggested_correction: Use the narrower supported point: Existing plots gave organizers capacity they could mobilize quickly. Alternatively supply a primary comparative study and state its actual scope.
findings.verification: source verification pending; do not label the historical proposition disproved

findings.quote: Everything in this chapter already exists
findings.reason: Later parts of this chapter explicitly discuss a future cleanup robot and research possibilities in health. The sentence is broader than the useful existing-tool examples that follow it.
findings.suggested_correction: Narrow the sentence to The tools introduced here already exist, and you can watch people build them. Keep the future and experimental labels in later sections.

findings.quote: printed on a $400 machine. it grows the fish food.
findings.reason: This embedded raster text survives after the surrounding prose became more careful. The definite fish-food claim suggests a completed replacement, while the next page says the prototype does not establish balanced-feed replacement. The $400 label also lacks a date or price basis in the current surrounding text. A Markdown-only text check cannot observe either embedded phrase.
findings.suggested_correction: Replace the baked-in subtitle with A home algae-culture experiment, or remove the subtitle and rely on the careful external caption. If retaining a price, source and date the historical printer price without implying project cost.
findings.verification: confirmed visually; price source verification pending, not claimed false

findings.quote: Some industrial vertical-farm vendors sell nearly identical hardware with the opposite pitch
findings.reason: The contrast relies on unnamed vendors, an uncited promotional claim and a hardware-equivalence assertion. The nearby citation supports the EasyGrow account, not an identifiable comparison with another vendor. Reducing labor also need not by itself establish the motive assigned here.
findings.suggested_correction: Name and cite one directly comparable vendor statement, then keep the inference distinct. Or make the contrast explicitly hypothetical and ask who receives the benefit when the same tools reduce labor.
findings.verification: source verification pending; vendor claim not independently checked

findings.reason: Chapter 11 has a section called The objections, answered once. Chapter 17 repeats the litter-responsibility objection and much of the wind/runoff explanation. The later section is strongest when it moves forward into a measurable cleanup procedure.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep the cleanup chain and comparison with existing crews, and shorten the repeated debate to an operational instruction to measure litter recurrence. A short pointer to Chapter 11 can preserve the connection.
findings.verification: confirmed by reading both complete passages

strengths: Scenes keep the knowledge distributed among the co-op and let physical consequences carry the argument.
The manuscript consistently distinguishes useful capacity from dependable access, and acknowledges labor, money and maintenance.
The soil trial and premortem retain unresolved limits instead of manufacturing a clean victory.
Most equations, figures, captions, lists and page continuations are legible; the principal production issue is page rhythm and citation treatment.

mechanical_validation.limit: These checks establish record completeness and byte binding. They cannot establish that an editor read or understood a page; that attestation is supplied only after the recorded direct review.
